title: Paleontologist Salary: How to Calculate Your Hourly Rate, Fortnightly Pay, and Annual Earnings
description: Understand paleontologist salary calculations: hourly to annual conversion, casual loading, super on top, tax brackets. Use our timesheet for your rate.
salarySummary: For a paleontologist earning $40 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross pay is $79,040 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the typical paleontologist salary in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single published figure for paleontologist salary from the Fair Work Commission or the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Most paleontologists are covered by a professional award or an enterprise agreement. You can use the ABS average weekly earnings for full-time adults ($2,083.70 per week as of May 2026) as a benchmark, but your actual rate depends on your employer, location, and experience. Enter your hourly rate into our timesheet to see your annual estimate.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: If you are a casual employee, the Fair Work Ombudsman requires a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, so a casual worker gets $33.05 per hour. Our timesheet has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. Remember that superannuation is paid on top of the casual rate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate shown on the timesheet?
faqs.a: No. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings and is paid on top of your hourly rate. It is not deducted from your pay. The Australian Taxation Office sets a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year for super guarantee purposes. Our calculator shows super as a separate estimated amount.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a full‑time employee, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. For example, a paleontologist salary of $45 per hour would give an annual gross of $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920.

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and instantly see your weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures. You can also check the box to add casual loading.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38‑hour week. This is the minimum for award/agreement‑free employees. Most paleontologists will be covered by a modern award, such as the Professional Employees Award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, updated after the Annual Wage Review. In 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%.

If you are a casual worker, you receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this works for award rates too.

## Fortnightly Pay and the 38‑Hour Week

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a paleontologist on $40 per hour, 38 hours per week: weekly = $1,520, fortnightly = $3,040. The [reference tables](/data) on this site show common conversions.

## Tax and Superannuation

Your take‑home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator uses these rates (with the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds for singles).

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a paleontologist earning $88,920, the employer would contribute an extra $10,670.40 into your super fund. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## Paleontologist Salary in Context

There is no single published figure for a paleontologist salary from the Fair Work Commission or the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full‑time adult employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 annually. However, this covers all occupations. Paleontologists often work in universities, museums, or consulting firms, and their pay may be set by enterprise agreements or individual contracts. To get a personalised estimate, enter your hourly rate into our [the timesheet](/) and adjust for your hours.

## Using the Calculator

Our timesheet is the home page. Type your base hourly rate into the field. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading – do not type a rate that already includes loading. The calculator will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super. It assumes 38 hours per week unless you change the hours field.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For award‑specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. For the National Minimum Wage and special rates, see the Fair Work Commission’s [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.
